newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat in thin range trade.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end flat in thin range trade.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished flat on Thursday after recovering from early lows following Wall Street's sharp overnight losses.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract added 10 points to close at 18,095 after hitting a low of 17,940. Market turnover was a thin 11,265 lots.
Dealers said the June Nikkei was buoyed by bargain-hunting interest near its lows but failed to climb above 18,170 as players cashed in their gains.

"People were afraid the Dow would go down again tonight. Everyone's very jittery. But I think we could see some U.S. funds moving back into the Japanese market, especially into high-tech stocks," said a trader at a Japanese futures house.
"I wouldn't be surprised if the market tries for a high of 18,400 tomorrow," he said, adding, however, that the June Nikkei was unlikely to climb much beyond that level in the near term.

Dealers said market fears of a near-term rate hike in Japan had subsided after the central bank's tankan survey on Wednesday showed sentiment among non-manufacturers remained wary despite a more upbeat mood among large manufacturers.
The Nikkei market's quiet session caused some locals to move into the Taiwan index futures pit where the April MSCI Taiwan index ended at 345.3 against its opening 336.0 on volume of 1,769 lots.
Dealers said the market rose on sharp gains in Taipei stocks, which benefitted from hopes that an easing of rules on bank shareholdings would draw new capital into the market.
Finance Minister Paul Chiu said Taipei would allow banks to hold 20 percent of their net asset value in stocks, up from 15 percent, effective in July.
Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary that news Taiwan planned to approve direct Taiwan-China shipping routes and that such sailings could begin within 10 days also boosted the market.
